summary: Submission approvable with 1 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

findings.details: Article's third 'What We Know' bullet states: '[Shacknews] reports the games are available to subscribers of any Xbox Game Pass tier, and players can also buy them individually.' The Shacknews snapshot (source-2.html.gz) confirms Game Pass tier availability ('Backwards compatible games will be available to subscribers of any Xbox Game Pass tier') but contains no mention of individual purchase, buying, or purchasing anywhere in the article text (verified via keyword search: zero hits for 'purchas', 'buy', 'individually'). The individual-purchase fact is true and is actually stated by Xbox Wire ('Each of these games is now available for purchase on PC') and by TheSixthAxis ('now to purchase on PC') — it is simply cited to the wrong outlet. Filed as a corrections record rather than a rejection because the underlying fact is accurate and independently verifiable in the other two cited sources.

content_preview.title: Microsoft Launches Xbox Backward Compatibility for PC, Starting With Four Classic Original Xbox Games
content_preview.summary: Microsoft brought Xbox Backward Compatibility to PC on July 22, letting Windows 11 and handheld owners play four original Xbox games for the first time.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft's Xbox division rolled out Xbox Backward Compatibility on PC on July 22, 2026, bringing classic original Xbox titles to Windows 11 machines and PC handhelds for the first time, according to [Xbox Wire](https://news.xbox.com/en-us/2026/07/22/xbox-backward-compatibility-on-pc/). The early-release launch starts with four games — BLiNX: The Time Sweeper, Conker: Live and Reloaded, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge, and Fuzion Frenzy — as confirmed by [Xbox Wire](https://news...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News-category piece using the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. 546 words, within the 400-1200 word range for News. The one-paragraph Analysis section is clearly labeled and reads as reasonable editorial interpretation (framing the PC rollout as an early-release test of emulation/licensing plumbing) rather than unsupported speculation presented as fact.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources were fetched successfully by chief_editor_review.ts (no archive_fallback, no failed snapshots) and I read every snapshot directly from the gzip files on disk after independently re-hashing each to confirm sha256 integrity against manifest.json (all three matched exactly): (1) sources/2026-07/microsoft-launches-xbox-backward-compatibility-for-pc-starting-with-four-classic-original-xbox-games/source-0.html.gz (news.xbox.com, the official Xbox Wire post) — confirms the July 22, 2026 launch date, the 'first time ever' framing for PC/handheld play, all four launch titles by exact name, the Jason Ronald quote verbatim ('Your library is more than just a collection of games. It is your personal history of epic stories and treasured memories from the past.') with his exact title 'VP of Next Generation, XBOX', Game Pass inclusion and console-to-PC license carryover, Play Anywhere/Cloud Gaming support, the exact graphics-customization list (4x resolution upscaling, VSync, Fullscreen/Windowed, anisotropic filtering, enhanced anti-aliasing), ROG Xbox Ally/Ally X handheld support, the exact minimum and recommended system requirements (post-edit figures — the page carries an 'Editor's Note (July 22): We've updated the minimum/recommended specs' — the article correctly cites the updated numbers), and the later-2026 Achievements plan plus intent to add more titles over time. Every claim attributed to Xbox Wire in the submission checks out verbatim or as a faithful paraphrase. (2) source-1.html.gz (thesixthaxis.com) — independently confirms the same four game titles, ROG Xbox Ally/Ally X support, Game Pass + license carryover, graphics customization, and later-2026 Achievements addition; TheSixthAxis's own reprinted minimum-spec figures are an older pre-edit version (e.g. Intel Core i3-8100 vs. Xbox Wire's updated i3-10300), but the submission does not attribute specs to TheSixthAxis, only to Xbox Wire, so this does not create a misattribution in the article. (3) source-2.html.gz (shacknews.com) — confirms the same four titles, Game Pass tier availability, and the new PC graphics settings, but does NOT mention individual purchase availability anywhere in the article text (confirmed by keyword search for 'purchas', 'buy', 'individually' — zero matches). The submission attributes 'players can also buy them individually' to Shacknews, which is a misattribution — flagged as a finding above and covered by a corrections record, since the fact itself is true and independently confirmed by both Xbox Wire and TheSixthAxis. No live WebFetch fallback was needed; all three snapshots saved successfully and were used as the canonical text for this review.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific number, name, quote, and date in the article traces to at least one of the three cited sources. The single exception is the Shacknews attribution issue documented above and in the findings array, which is a citation-to-wrong-outlet problem for a true, independently-verifiable fact — not a fabrication. No hallucinated facts, no invented quotes, no invented figures.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no promotional language, no AI self-reference. The Analysis section is appropriately hedged ('suggests', 'the kind of foundation it can build on') rather than asserting unsupported conclusions as fact.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior coverage of Xbox backward compatibility on PC — none found. Two other July 2026 Xbox-related articles exist in the archive (09-xbox-confirms-3200-job-cuts-... and 20-us-and-canadian-game-worker-unions-file-unfair-labor-practice-charges-...), both about layoffs/labor disputes and unrelated to this backward-compatibility feature launch. A March 2026 article on 'Project Helix' (a rumored future Xbox/PC hybrid console) touches on a related long-term Xbox/PC convergence theme but covers a distinct, separate story (a prospective new console architecture, not today's software backward-compatibility feature for existing PCs). This is genuinely new, non-duplicate coverage. Note: PR #2025 reportedly covers the same underlying news event from a different contributor bot submission opened later; per instructions this PR (#2016) was opened first and is being reviewed on its own merits, with the duplicate to be resolved by #2025's reviewer deferring.
editor_notes.human_requested_review: N/A — human_requested is false for this submission; no heightened-scrutiny checklist applies, though full source verification was performed regardless per standing editorial policy.
concerns: One 'What We Know' bullet misattributes the individual-purchase-availability fact to Shacknews when Shacknews's article does not state it; the fact is true and is actually sourced from Xbox Wire and TheSixthAxis. Addressed via a corrections record rather than rejection since it is a single, isolated citation error and the substance is accurate.

thesixthaxis.com and shacknews.com are not in config/source_allowlist.txt. Both are long-running, bylined gaming-news outlets with clear editorial identity, correction/comment policies, and independent reporting (not aggregators or content farms); I assessed them as reputable for this story despite the allowlist gap and recommend adding them to the allowlist rather than treating this as a rejection-worthy source-quality issue.
recommendations: File a corrections record clarifying that the individual-purchase-availability fact is sourced from Xbox Wire / TheSixthAxis, not Shacknews.
Add news.xbox.com's companion outlets thesixthaxis.com and shacknews.com to config/source_allowlist.txt given their established editorial track record in games journalism.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, neutral News piece on a genuinely new story. One isolated, minor source misattribution (an accurate fact credited to the wrong of three cited outlets) is the only defect found after reading all three source snapshots in full; it does not touch the headline, summary, or lead, and is honestly coverable in a single corrections entry. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
